messages:
mike: heads up — noticed memory creeping on long-context runs, looks like kv cache pages are being reused incorrectly across requests. repro on prod-dedicated-3 with 100k token session :eyes:
anya: hmm. any logs or a small repro?
sam: how much creeping? steady growth or spikes after certain ops?
mike: steady growth until oom in ~45m for one worker. I dumped kvpage meta, see overlapping offsets between requests:
```
KV_PAGE 0: used=8192 free=0 owner=req-91 start_offset=0 end_offset=4096 tag=0x1a2b
KV_PAGE 0: owner=req-92 start_offset=2048 end_offset=6144 tag=0x1a2b
```
That `owner` flip looks wrong — same page being appended without eviction.
ravi: that looks like cross-request append, maybe we missed clearing the page owner after eviction. Could be race with async writeback.
anya: any correlation with batching or kernel changes? we shipped batching heuristic tweak yesterday (reduce max_batch_size to favor latency).
mike: last good deploy was before that tweak. timeline aligns. but why would batching affect page ownership? maybe we changed how we pin pages for in-flight requests.
sam: can you run the reproducer with `KV_DEBUG=1` and `--no-batching` to isolate? also get a lightweight heap profile.
mike: running now. repro command I used: `python tools/long_context_repro.py --tokens 100000 --concurrency 2 --model redwood/gptx-13b`
(quick logs)
```
[14:22:10] req-91 append 2048 -> page0
[14:22:11] req-92 append 0 -> page0
[14:22:11] eviction trigger, but owner not cleared for page0
[14:22:12] req-93 append 4096 -> page0
```
So page0 is getting interleaved appends from multiple requests.
anya: that smells like wrong alignment calculation when we compute `append_offset = (page_base + (token_idx % page_size))` — if token_idx is global rather than per-request it can collide.
ravi: good call. i found a code path in `kv/append.rs` where we use `global_token_counter.fetch_add(n)` for offset calc during batching. should be per-request sequence.
sam: if it's global and we batch, concurrent requests will reserve offsets out-of-order causing overlaps. that explains why disabling batching might hide it.
mike: disabling batching with `--no-batching` stops the overlap in my run. confirming batching is the catalyst.
anya: ok fix plan: change reserve to use per-request local seq, or introduce reservation slots in page metadata with an owner field set atomically. which is less invasive?
ravi: adding atomic owner + length compare is smaller change: when we reserve, CAS page.owner from 0->reqid with expected free range. if CAS fails, retry. that'll avoid global counter.
sam: add tests: multi-threaded repro harness that asserts no two reqids touch same page range. also add a stress test that runs for 1m with high concurrency.
mike: i'll draft the PR. rough patch idea:
```diff
- let o = GLOBAL_TOKEN_COUNTER.fetch_add(n, SeqCst);
+ let o = req_ctx.local_seq.fetch_add(n, SeqCst);
```
but ravi's CAS approach might be less churn.
ravi: i'll prototype CAS approach and run against long_context_repro. If green, push as hotfix to dedicated-stable ring.
deploy-bot: deploy started: kvfix/cas-reserve -> dedicated-stable (by ravi)
mike: thanks. also found some stale blocks lingering after request ends — we should ensure cleanup path clears `page.tag` and zeroes metadata. logged as follow-up ticket.
anya: create the ticket and link here. pls include trace snippets and heap profile.
mike: created ticket INF-789: "kvpage owner leak after overlapping append" with steps and logs. added heap profile: peak RSS +45MB on 100k token run.
sam: postmortem checklist: root cause = wrong reservation semantics when batching -> overlapping appends -> stale owner/tag left on pages -> cross-request contamination + memory growth. mitigation: hotfix CAS owner reservation, add unit+stress tests, enhance CI to run long_context_repro nightly.
ravi: running stress with CAS patch now, 10 runs so far no overlap. will open PR and request review.
mike: if reviewers ok, let's canary to dedicated-beta, keep 1% traffic for 24h.
anya: assign reviewers: @sam, @anya. also add commit message linking INF-789.
sam: ack. I can review later today. :thumbsup:
mike: logging note — added extra kv meta dump command: `tools/kv_inspect.py --page 0 --full` which prints owner/tag ranges. use that when debugging.
ravi: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/kv/compare/kv-cas-reserve. added tests.
mike: great. moving to monitor. thanks everyone.
